Good table
Dec 2025 • Couples
Stoker stands out as a serious and accepted address for quality meat lovers. The menu, which is very educational, details the cuts, the methods of cooking over a wood fire and the principle of dry-aging, reflecting a real culture of the product and an appreciable transparency.
The piece served, an impressive tomahawk with remarkable wigging, is presented raw at the table, on a board stamped, before cooking. A simple but effective ritual that inspires confidence. Cooking, precisely, was perfectly controlled, respecting to the letter the degree requested and fully enhancing the quality of the meat.
Important point to note for European customers: vegetables and starches are not included with meat, as is often the practice in Belgium. We must not forget to order them as an accompaniment.
The service is quality, attentive and professional, with good advice on both pieces and cooking or accompaniments. The whole gives the impression of mastery and consistency: here, meat is clearly at the center of the experience.
However, prices are high for Vietnam, but consistent with the positioning, product quality and level of service offered.
A convincing address for lovers of beautiful pieces, provided you accept the budget.

Nice Setting and Service - But Steaks Fell Short
Jul 2025 • Family
I had high hopes for our dinner at Stoker Woodfired Grill & Bar in Ho Chi Minh City. With its strong ratings on TripAdvisor and a mention in the Michelin Guide, it was one of the few restaurants I had marked as a must-visit on our trip to Vietnam. The space itself is warm and stylish, with a modern, upscale ambiance that immediately set the tone for what we expected to be a memorable steakhouse experience.

The bread service was a surprising standout—beautifully baked, flavorful, and served warm. A clear 5/5.

For starters, we tried the Wagyu Beef Tartare, which was beautifully plated and absolutely delicious. Another strong 5/5.

Unfortunately, the mains - the steaks - left us underwhelmed, especially for a restaurant that brands itself around wood-fired grilling.

- The grain-fed ribeye my son ordered had a nice char and good flavor overall. However, he requested medium rare, but it arrived clearly rare. Still enjoyable, but a miss on execution. (4/5)
- I ordered the grass-fed ribeye, asking for rare plus. It came out closer to medium, with no discernible char and surprisingly little flavor. It lacked the depth and smokiness you'd expect from a wood-fired steak. (1/5)
- My daughter ordered the filet, medium rare, but it arrived more medium, and was unfortunately bland. It was so underwhelming that she didn’t even want to finish it. (1/5)

When you go to a steakhouse, you expect the steaks to be the hero of the meal, unfortunately for our experience they were the weakest part. It was disappointing, especially given the restaurant’s reputation and premium pricing.

Mixed Experience at Stokers
Nov 2019 • Friends
I have visited Stokers twice now. The first time I was blown away and would have given a 5 star rating. The service is very good and the food was absolutely delicious. We ate a wondeful smoked flavour soup, steak with flavoursome chimichurra sauce and fries and I ordered a pear and rocket salad and woodfired cauliflower with mustard and parmesan cheese. The salad was delightful, the dressing delicate and the shaved pear worked so well with the rocket. And the woodfired cauliflower was quite literally the most tasty vegetable I have ever eaten anywhere. I had a dessert with cherries but would rather thar the cherries had been sharp to counterbalance the rest of the very sweet dessert but it was still pleasant enough. So what went wrong during the second visit? Well the staff were still great though not quick to clear the tables of empty bottles etc but the pumpkin soup was so thick it was more like a steak sauce than a soup but even thicker and stodgier than that even. It was still delicious but not a welcome thickness or texture. The accompanying bread with cheese and onions was still very tasty though. Then the main course - the steak and chimichurra sauce were fine as were the french fries but the cartots and veg were scarcely luke warm so I asked for them to be returned hot. In fairness they were heated up shortly after. Then the woodfired cauliflower arrived, also barely luke warm so I requested that the cauliflower was also reheated. I had completely eaten my food by the time the cauliflower was brought back and this time nstead of being luke warm the caulifower was cool, verging on being cold. I was particularly disappointed with the cauliflower as it had been so wonderful the time before. So I asked for a take away so I could heat the cauliflower at home later that day. Had this been the first time I visited Stokers I would never have gone back but I still have this wondeful memory of the food when I visited the first time - which was perfection. So I will go again as hopefully the problems associated with the second time were just a hitch. The overall rating for the 2 dining experiences combined should really be a Good but the rating only offers Very Good or Average so I opted for Average as the second visit couldn't justify a Very Good rating overall. Fingers crossed for a 3rd experience like the 1st one.

Did This Fine Dining Restaurant 'Wow' Its Guests? It's The Details That Count!
Jun 2016 • Friends
Walking into Stoker Woodfire Grill & Bar I had no expectations. I hadn't heard anything good or bad about it, and so stepping into the fine dining environment that it is began to quick establish expectations. Immediately I expected exceptional service excellence delivery, proactive attentiveness to our needs and a menu and taste that matches the environment. 
The menu is one of the most pricey in HCMC. With that comes expectations and deliverables critical to the guest experience. 
Table arrangements - not the most private, as groups of different guests need sit beside each other when capacity reaches its peak. 
Fine Dining Table Service - did our host put offer to put the napkin on our lap - no. Did the hostess refill our glasses with the bottle of wine we had ordered - no.
The same plate used for the bread was also required to be used for the main meal. I would have thought a change of plate would have been in order even though we were sharing meat dishes.This is where proactive and attentive service was required.
Menu - a chid was in our group - did the restaurant menu accommodate for a younger diner either in menu choice or in offering to accommodate for smaller dishes - no. 
There was some misunderstanding regarding what we ordered 'ribs on the bone'. We received one rib but expected multiple ribs as the menu was plural. 
Accompanying Breads - did the bread offering accommodate for the group of four or did the bread offering stay the same for how many were in a group? Stayed the same no matter we were two or four people. 
Attentiveness to requests - we requested balsamic vinegar to accompany our bread. Did this come to our table? No. After a reminder was made to the hostess did it come to our table? No.
Taste - the meal was cooked to perfection. As ordered and tasted delicious. The accompanying sauces for the meats were a delight and truly scrumptious. 
Management Visit - should we have expected in such a fine dining establishment that the manager on duty or chef would have visited our table to enquire if our meal was delicious and to our liking? yes. Did they do that? No.

Overall summary - In such an establishment we should have expected to be 'wowed' on all fronts and the restaurant failed to deliver. The food is dam good - but the attention to details as should have been expected in regards to service excellence delivery are lacking. An enjoyable night overall.
